items.t: Zacks Research Expects Higher Earnings for Gilead Sciences
sum: - Zacks Research повысила прогноз прибыли на акцию для Gilead Sciences на первый квартал 2027 года до $2,10 с $2,09, сохранив при этом рекомендацию «Держать»; По оценкам компании, прибыль на акцию на 2027 финансовый год составит $9,42.

- Последние квартальные результаты Gilead превзошли ожидания: прибыль на акцию составила $2,55 против консенсус-прогноза в $2,19, а выручка в $8,30 млрд превзошла прогнозы и выросла на 6,8% в годовом исчислении.
- Настроения аналитиков в целом позитивные: консенсус «умеренная покупка» и средняя целевая цена $171,07; 23 аналитика рекомендуют акции «Покупать», а шесть – «Держать».

Gilead Sciences, Inc. (NASDAQ:GILD — бесплатный отчет) — Аналитики Zacks Research повысили оценки прибыли на акцию (EPS) в первом квартале 2027 года для акций Gilead Sciences в аналитической записке, опубликованной в четверг, 12 ноября. Аналитическая группа Zacks Research теперь прогнозирует, что биофармацевтическая компания заработает $2,10 на акцию за квартал по сравнению с предыдущим прогнозом в $2,09. В настоящее время Zacks Research рекомендует держать акции компании. Консенсус-оценка текущей годовой прибыли Gilead Sciences составляет (0,98 доллара) на акцию. Zacks Research также опубликовала оценки прибыли Gilead Sciences во втором квартале 2027 года на уровне $2,25 на акцию, в третьем квартале 2027 года на уровне $2,49 на акцию, прибыли на акцию в 2027 финансовом году на уровне $9,42 на акцию, прибыли во втором квартале 2028 года на уровне $2,32 на акцию, прибыли в третьем квартале 2028 года на уровне $2,58 на акцию и прибыли в 2028 финансовом году на уровне $9,69 на акцию.

GILD был предметом нескольких других исследовательских отчетов. Morgan Stanley повысил целевую цену акций Gilead Sciences с $163,00 до $183,00 и присвоил акциям рейтинг «выше рынка» в исследовательской записке в пятницу, 30 октября. Barclays снизил целевую цену на акции Gilead Sciences с $155,00 до $145,00 и установил для акций рейтинг «равного веса» в аналитической записке в среду, 29 июля. HSBC повысил целевую цену акций Gilead Sciences со $155,00 до $175,00 и присвоил акциям рекомендацию «покупать» в своем отчете в четверг, 10 сентября. Сэнфорд С. Бернштейн подтвердил рейтинг «лучше рынка» и в аналитической записке в понедельник, 2 ноября, установил целевую цену на акции Gilead Sciences в размере $175,00. Наконец, Кантор Фицджеральд повысил целевую цену акций Gilead Sciences с $155,00 до $175,00 и присвоил компании рейтинг «выше рынка» в своем отчете в пятницу, 30 октября.

items.t: Gilead (GILD) Stock Still Looks Undervalued On Its 205% Run
sum: Gilead Sciences has ridden a powerful run in recent years, with the stock now trading near US$170.87, so the key question is whether that share price still matches what its cash flows can support. With major HIV and liver disease programs in the spotlight again, investors are increasingly asking how the company's current valuation lines up against the cash the business can realistically generate.
- Over the past 5 years the stock has returned about 205.2%, which puts a lot of accumulated optimism on the line if the underlying cash generation story does not keep pace.

- Fresh data around treatments such as lenacapavir for HIV prevention, Livdelzi for primary biliary cholangitis and new cellular therapies can reshape expectations for future revenue durability, margin quality and the timing of cash inflows that feed into any cash flow based valuation.
- If you'd rather focus on sales, this one's for you. See what Gilead Sciences's 6.8x P/S says about the price.
The stock's next move may depend on whether today's market price is adequately backed by the cash flows implied by a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of Gilead Sciences.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here focuses on the cash Gilead Sciences can return to shareholders over time. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $13.8b, and the projections assume that this pool of cash grows rather than shrinks over the next decade, with a second stage fading to steadier expansion after 2030. That kind of profile fits a mature pharmaceutical group that is still investing heavily in areas like HIV, liver disease and cell therapy.

Gilead Sciences stock gains a new signal from lenacapavir data
sum: Gilead Sciences added a concrete HIV prevention result to the pipeline debate on Friday, November 6, as the company released one-year PURPOSE 5 data ahead of presentations at HIV Glasgow. The study showed that twice-yearly lenacapavir kept more participants on PrEP than daily oral F/TDF, according to Gilead Sciences.

At Week 52, 85.6 percent of participants receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir remained persistent on PrEP, compared with 46.3 percent for daily F/TDF. The difference was statistically significant, and no HIV acquisitions occurred among participants receiving lenacapavir during the study period.

The Phase 2 trial enrolled people in the United Kingdom and France who were not taking PrEP at enrollment. Gilead said one HIV acquisition occurred in the F/TDF group, with drug-level analysis consistent with fewer than two doses per week at diagnosis.

The safety profile was broadly consistent with earlier studies. Serious adverse events occurred in 3.9 percent of participants receiving lenacapavir and 3.4 percent of those receiving F/TDF, while injection-site reactions were the most common treatment-related events for lenacapavir.

HIV Glasgow runs from Sunday, November 8, through Wednesday, November 11. Gilead is presenting more than 50 studies spanning prevention, treatment and cure research, including results on lenacapavir, Biktarvy, the investigational once-weekly islatravir-lenacapavir combination and GS-3242.

The PURPOSE 5 results strengthen the commercial case for less frequent dosing, but they do not remove clinical, regulatory, pricing or market-access risks. For investors, the conference offers evidence on persistence and treatment preferences rather than a confirmed near-term revenue contribution.

Gilead Sciences stock traded at 150.43 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:01 CET on Monday, November 9, 0.18 percent above the Xetra close of Friday, November 6. The comparison uses the last completed Xetra session because the European trading day had not reached the evening close threshold.

Is Liver Disease Trial Success Altering The Investment Case For Gilead Stock (GILD)?
sum: Gilead Sciences reported detailed Phase 3 IDEAL data showing Livdelzi helped a majority of primary biliary cholangitis patients reach the alkaline phosphatase normalization composite endpoint. HIV Glasgow 2026 presentations also highlighted twice-yearly lenacapavir and other programs across prevention, treatment and cure research.

Together, the Livdelzi and lenacapavir updates highlight how Gilead Sciences is trying to broaden revenue sources beyond core HIV regimens into liver disease and long acting prevention, while still carrying meaningful safety, pricing and market access considerations.
We will look at how Gilead Sciences’ investment narrative is influenced by Livdelzi’s Phase 3 success in primary biliary cholangitis.
Spot 35 healthcare AI stocks that, like Gilead Sciences, are trying to turn specialized therapies and long-acting treatments into durable revenue streams across complex chronic diseases.

To own Gilead Sciences, you need to believe the HIV engine can stay resilient while newer areas like liver disease and oncology steadily carry more of the load. The recent Livdelzi IDEAL data and HIV Glasgow line up both speak to that goal, but the near term story is still shaped by earnings volatility, high debt and acquired R&D charges that keep GAAP results in loss territory.

The most important short term catalysts revolve around execution in HIV long acting prevention and treatment, plus how quickly Livdelzi usage can build within its current label. Key near term risks remain pricing pressure on core HIV regimens, the firm’s heavy dependence on that franchise and the possibility that newer programs scale more slowly than hoped. If investors judge the latest data as incremental rather than transformative, the impact on those near term drivers may be modest.

The Livdelzi IDEAL readout looks most relevant for this discussion. Gilead Sciences now has detailed Phase 3 evidence that 75.4% of treated PBC patients in the trial achieved the ALP normalization composite endpoint at Week 52 versus 16.1% on placebo, with a safety profile described as consistent with prior studies. For an investor, that expands the clinical backbone behind an emerging liver portfolio that sits alongside HIV and oncology as a potential third business leg.

Was There Any Sign Gilead Stock Would Run?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Gilead Sciences (GILD) stock rose 30.9% between August 3 and October 30, 2026, while the S&P 500 ended those three months flat. During the run, Gilead reported two quarters of faster sales growth, with double-digit gains for its HIV drugs leading the first. Anticipating this rally meant hearing about the HIV growth and seeing sales pick up before August. So when did Gilead first give investors a reason to expect faster sales?

Management did so as early as its February 11, 2025 call, though the message was mixed. Executives said full-year HIV sales grew 8% in 2024 and that Gilead had filed for approval of lenacapavir for twice-yearly HIV prevention. On the same call, management flagged the impact of Medicare Part D reform on revenue growth. HIV growth was on the record early, and so was a Medicare change that management linked to revenue growth.

Regulatory filings then showed the pickup quarter by quarter, all of it public before the run. Revenue slipped 0.3% from a year earlier in the quarter ended March 2025, which Gilead filed on May 7, 2025. Growth then rose in each of the next three quarters, reaching 4.7% in the quarter ended December 2025. In the quarter ended March 2026, the last period filed before the run, growth eased to 4.4%.

More HIV news arrived in June 2026, though not about sales. On June 15, the FDA accepted the company’s application for a once-weekly pill form of Yeztugo, its lenacapavir drug, for HIV prevention. Over the wider stretch from February 2 to August 3, 2026, though, the shares fell 7.1%. A reader following the filings had the sales pickup in hand while the stock price went the other way.

Revenue in the quarter ended June 2026, reported on August 4, grew 10.2% from a year earlier. This compared with 1.8% in the same quarter of 2025. The June period also ended in a net loss of $10.5 billion, which news reports attributed to costs related to a series of acquisitions. Gilead returned to a profit in the quarter ended September. It still shows a net loss over the four quarters to September 2026, making its P/E not meaningful. Investors now pay 6.8 times sales for Gilead shares, against 3.2 times for the S&P 500, without a twelve-month profit behind that price.

sum: Gilead Sciences (GILD) has recently been on Zacks.com's list of the most searched stocks. Therefore, you might want to consider some of the key factors that could influence the stock's performance in the near future.

Over the past month, shares of this HIV and hepatitis C drugmaker have returned +5%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +0.5% change. During this period, the Zacks Medical - Biomedical and Genetics industry, which Gilead falls in, has gained 3.2%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Gilead is expected to post a loss of $7.09 per share, indicating a change of -452.7% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -0.7% over the last 30 days.

Is the Bearishness Around Pfizer and Gilead Sciences a Contrarian Opportunity?
sum: Both Pfizer and Gilead Sciences just flashed the same ominous technical warning while trading below analyst fair value, but the reasons behind each selloff tell very different stories about which one actually deserves a second look.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Pfizer (NYSE:PFE | PFE Price Prediction) trades at $24.25, against a Wall Street consensus price target of $28.79, which represents implied upside of almost 19%. Gilead Sciences (NASDAQ:GILD) trades at $130.04 and has a $158.30 consensus target. Both stocks sit below sell-side fair value while flashing the same bearish technical warning.

Pfizer and Gilead Sciences are widely held large-cap pharma names, popular for yield, defensive characteristics, and late-stage pipelines. Investors are paying attention because both have seen a so-called death cross, the pattern where a stock’s 50-day moving average slips beneath the 200-day average. Pfizer’s 50-day is at 25.35, versus a 200-day of 25.87. Gilead’s 50-day is 129.85 against a 200-day of 130.44.

A death cross is a lagging indicator that says nothing on its own about valuation. Still, both names trade below analyst fair value with momentum rolling over. That puts the contrarian question squarely on the table.

Pfizer’s weakness is the COVID hangover colliding with a policy overhang. Recent results still show growth, with quarterly revenue up 5.4% year over year. Yet the market is fixated on Most-Favored-Nation drug pricing, potential Section 232 pharma tariffs, the IRA Medicare Part D redesign, and international Eliquis generic entry. Management has also signaled no share buybacks in 2026, removing a support pillar.

Gilead’s story is more complex. First-quarter revenue topped expectations, but the company slashed non-GAAP EPS guidance from a profit of $8.45 to $8.85 down to a loss of $0.65 to $1.05, driven by roughly $11.5 billion in IPR&D charges tied to the Arcellx, Ouro Medicines, and Tubulis acquisitions. Those are non-cash accounting items, but Wall Street hated the optics. Add in Trodelvy’s ASCENT-07 primary endpoint miss and Veklury revenue dropping 52% year over year, and momentum turned quickly.

Nurix Stock Up 29% in a Month: Here's What You Should Know
sum: Shares of Nurix Therapeutics NRIX have seen a sharp increase over the past month, primarily driven by growing investor optimism about the company's recently announced collaboration with Swiss pharma giant Roche RHHBY.
Shares of Nurix have rallied 28.6% in the past month compared with the industry's increase of 2.5%.

Earlier this month, the companies signed an exclusive licensing and collaboration agreement to co-develop and co-commercialize one of Nurix's lead pipeline candidates, bexobrutideg (NX-5948), across various malignant hematology, immunology and neurology indications.

Per the deal, Nurix is entitled to receive $700 million upfront and could earn up to $2.3 billion in total through development, regulatory, and commercial milestone payments from RHHBY. While Nurix will fund 40% of development costs, Roche will be covering the remaining 60%.

However, the companies will equally share all profits and losses from net sales of the product upon potential approval and launch in the United States. In ex-U.S. markets, Roche will solely lead all commercialization activities, and Nurix will receive tiered royalties ranging from the low to high-teens

The partnership is looking to build on Nurix's pioneering expertise in targeted protein degradation with Roche's leading portfolio of B-cell targeted therapies and clinical and commercial infrastructure.

Bexobrutideg is an investigational, orally bioavailable, brain-penetrant Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) degrader being developed for the treatment of relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies, as well as immunology and neurology indications. It uses a novel protein degradation mechanism that eliminates BTK rather than simply inhibiting it, potentially overcoming resistance associated with currently available BTK inhibitors.

According to Yahoo Finance, Gilead reported second-quarter 2026 HIV sales of USD 5.70 billion, up 12.00 percent year over year. Total product sales reached USD 7.60 billion, up 8.00 percent year over year, while Trodelvy sales rose 26.00 percent to USD 457.00 million.

Management raised full-year 2026 HIV sales growth guidance to 9.00-10.00 percent from 8.00 percent previously. The company also projected total product sales of USD 30.10-30.40 billion, while cell therapy sales were expected to decline by a mid-teens percentage.

The Tradegate substitute quote of EUR 127.62 on October 6, 2026 places the stock below the primary Nasdaq 52-week high of USD 157.29 and above the low of USD 112.82. The currencies and venues are separate, so the Nasdaq range does not measure the euro quote directly.

As Gilead's Trodelvy stumbles in first-line lung cancer, all eyes turn to Merck, AZ and Daiichi rivals
sum: Following another phase 3 failure for Gilead Sciences’ Trodelvy, the race to bring a TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) to patients with first-line non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has narrowed.

Monday, Merck & Co. and Gilead announced that they are pulling the plug on the phase 3 Evoke-03 trial, also known as Keynote-D46, following the recommendation of an external data monitoring committee.
The study was evaluating Trodelvy, combined with Keytruda, as a first-line treatment in patients with PD-L1-high NSCLC versus Keytruda alone.

The trial did not meet its progression-free survival endpoint at its final analysis, even though a positive trend was observed, according to the two companies. Additionally, an interim analysis of overall survival suggested the trial was unlikely to achieve statistical significance on this measure.

The Evoke-03 flop deals another major blow to the first-in-class TROP2 ADC following a second-line NSCLC trial setback more than two years ago. Gilead’s stock price dropped about 2.7% as of publication time Tuesday morning.

Without a win in first-line NSCLC, Trodelvy’s commercial future will mainly depend on its triple-negative breast cancer uses, which won’t be able to justify the $21 billion price tag that Gilead paid for the med’s developer, Immunomedics. Gilead already took major write-offs tied to Trodelvy’s second-line NSCLC failure and a market withdrawal in bladder cancer in 2024.

Trodelvy’s latest PFS miss surprised analysts at Jefferies and Leerink Partners. For the broader oncology industry, the Evoke-03 failure serves as a warning that “beating the easy [Keytruda] monotherapy standard-of-care (SoC) as an entry into 1L NSCLC may not be as easy as it seems,” the Leerink team wrote in a June 8 note.

sum: - 2025 results: Total product sales were $28.9 billion, up 1% and above guidance, with base-business sales (ex‑Veklury) up 4% — or roughly 8% growth excluding the Medicare Part D redesign headwind.

- HIV momentum and Sunlenca launch: HIV sales were $20.8 billion (+6%) driven by Biktarvy and prevention growth; the twice‑yearly injectable Sunlenca (Yes2Go) generated $150 million in 2025, reached ~90% payer coverage, and management forecasts about $800 million in revenue for 2026.

- Pipeline and 2026 guidance: Gilead plans multiple potential launches in 2026 (including Trodelvy first‑line TNBC, a bictegravir+lenacapavir oral combo, anito‑cel, and bulevirtide) and guided product sales of $29.6–30.0 billion with non‑GAAP EPS of $8.45–8.85 despite Veklury declines, pricing headwinds and competition in cell therapy.

Pfizer sells its stake in GSK's ViiV for $1.9B, with Shionogi upping its ante in the HIV-focused company
sum: Five weeks after telling investors to expect a revenue decline in 2026, Pfizer has found a quick funding fix, selling off its stake in GSK’s ViiV Healthcare.

The New York powerhouse has agreed to surrender its 11.7% interest in the HIV-focused company for $1.875 billion. Under terms of the agreement, Shionogi will pick up Pfizer’s shares for $2.125 billion, with GSK gaining a special dividend of $250 million.

The deal allows majority owner GSK to retain its 78.3% interest in ViiV, while Osaka, Japan-based Shionogi will boost its stake in ViiV from 10% to 21.7%. The companies expect to close the deal in the first quarter of this year.

“This agreement simplifies ViiV’s shareholder structure and we look forward to continuing our highly successful collaboration with Shionogi to advance ViiV’s pipeline and portfolio of long-acting injectable HIV treatment and prevention medicines,” ViiV Chairman David Redfern said in a release.

Also as part of the deal, Shionogi will retain its one director position on the ViiV board, currently occupied by John Keller, Ph.D., who has been in place since Shionogi gained a stake in ViiV in 2012.

“Shionogi is dedicated to addressing major infectious diseases, with HIV being one of our most important focus areas, as reflected by our role in the discovery of the innovative integrase inhibitors dolutegravir and cabotegravir,” Keller, also the chief of R&D at Shionogi, added in the release.

GSK and Pfizer launched ViiV in 2009 to discover new medicines to combat HIV and provide better resources for people with AIDS. At the time, GSK took an 85% stake in ViiV, with Pfizer holding the other 15%. In 2012, ViiV acquired Shionogi’s HIV portfolio in exchange for royalty committments and a 10% stake in the company.
